history.period: Said to be as old as the city of Jalandhar - UNVERIFIED
history.summary: This ancient temple in the Kot Kishan Chand locality is built in honour of Vrinda (Tulsi), the chaste wife of the demon Jalandhara after whom the city is named; a tank beside the temple is traditionally Jalandhara's bathing place. The Sheetla Mandir near the Balmiki gate is said to be as old as the city itself, and the precincts hold two small old temples of Hanuman and Shiva plus a nearby Gupha temple with an Annapurna shrine and a Brahm Kund. No verifiable construction date or patron is documented, so the ancient-dating claims are UNVERIFIED. Coordinates geocoded to the Vrinda Devi Temple address (relevance 90); no festivals found documented for this temple.

name: Tulsi Mandir
town_description: Jalandhar is one of Punjab's oldest cities, its name linked in legend to the demon Jalandhara whose tank bathes the city's ancient temples; it is a major Doaba-region commercial centre on NH-44. The Tulsi Mandir stands in the Kot Kishan Chand locality in the old city. The surrounding Brahm Kund, Shiva shrines and Sheetla Mandir form one of the oldest religious quarters of Jalandhar.
